main_text.p: ceperit ipse ac recondi-derit, id ipsum quaerere solet, reperire autem non potest. Quúmque nun-ciatur illi obiisse aliquem ex familiaribus ipsius, ut veniat exequias, tum ille vultu ad mœstitiam composito, lacrymas e-tiam fundens, Bene, inquit, eveniat. Debitas autem pecunias recipiens, testes sibi asciscit: & vigente hyeme, cum famulo quod cucumeres non emerit, iurgatur. Puerulos quinetiam suos, ut lucta se exerceant, cursu contendant, usque ad fatigationem cogere solet. In agro lentem ipse coquens, sale bis in ollam iniecto, ut mâdi nequeat efficit. cumque à Ioue pluit, Sane quàm, inquit, siderum aqua suauis mihi videtur.ψυχρὸν νομίζεις, ὅτι ἀὴρ [?] ......

page.notes: Greek column: several words are doubtful and marked [?], especially the first word, the word at the end of line 6 and 7, and the word "ἠρόεασε". The symbol "©" before "εἰς" is kept as printed. The Latin column reads "poteft" in the print; it is given as "potest" because the long s is plain s. The last Greek line is only partly visible in the scan. Greek marginal note at the left, transcribed from a pale and partly faded print; its accents and final letters are uncertain. The text opens mid-paragraph, so the first paragraph continues from the previous part.
